android.why: Google Sign-In's own service, behind Google's signature permission.

android.title: Broadcast Receiver (androidx.profileinstaller.ProfileInstallReceiver) is Protected by a permission, but the protection level of the permission should be checked. Permission: android.permission.DUMP [android:exported=true]

android.title: App uses SQLite Database and execute raw SQL query. Untrusted user input in raw SQL queries can cause SQL Injection. Also sensitive information should be encrypted and written to the database.
android.why: SQLCipher and capacitor-sqlite internals. Gleam's store binds every value.

android.title: The App uses an insecure Random Number Generator.
android.why: Library code. Keys and nonces come from WebCrypto.

android.title: Files may contain hardcoded sensitive information like usernames, passwords, keys etc.
android.why: Library constants such as option names, not credentials.

android.title: App can read/write to External Storage. Any App can read data written to External Storage.
android.why: Capacitor Filesystem. Gleam writes only to its private cache.

android.title: App creates temp file. Sensitive information should never be written into a temp file.
SHA-1 is a weak hash known to have hash collisions.
android.why: capacitor-sqlite's JSON export encryption, which Gleam doesn't use.

Raw HTML injection sink detected (dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, outerHTML, document.write, or insertAdjacentHTML). In hybrid mobile apps and WebViews, DOM XSS can escalate to native bridge access.
android.why: React DOM internals. Gleam's code has no HTML sinks.
